concept.name: Median
concept.definition: The middle value of an ordered data set: the point with half the observations below it and half above. For an even number of observations it is conventionally the average of the two central values.
concept.intuition: It is the 'typical middle' value that ignores how extreme the tails are. Half the data lies on each side, by construction.
concept.mechanics: Sort the data ascending; if N is odd, take the ((N+1)/2)th value; if N is even, average the (N/2)th and (N/2 + 1)th values. Because it depends only on ranks, it is robust to outliers and skew.
concept.formula: For ordered data Y_(1) <= ... <= Y_(N): median = Y_((N+1)/2) if N is odd; median = (Y_(N/2) + Y_(N/2 + 1))/2 if N is even.
concept.failure_modes: By discarding magnitude information, the median can hide important tail behavior - two return series with the same median can have very different crash risk. It is also less statistically efficient than the mean when data truly are normal.
concept.misconceptions: The median is not necessarily a member of the data set, and it equals the mean only for symmetric distributions; for skewed data they differ systematically, with the mean pulled toward the long tail.
concept.example: For trade P&Ls of -50, -20, 10, 30, 400, the median is 10 while the mean is 74; the single large win dominates the mean but leaves the median unchanged.
